A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Diffusion Blend, with matching core methods and substantial retained content. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the substantial additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, reward measurements, inference timings and qualitative comparisons in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds evaluations of DB-MPA-LS, GenEval, conflicting rewards, reward-count scaling and SDXL in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 introduces DB-MPA-LS, which samples one reward-specific LoRA adapter per denoising step according to preference weights instead of evaluating and blending all models. This substantially changes inference computation. The original DB-MPA and DB-KLA procedures remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation on GenEval, extending coverage to counting, spatial relations and other compositional tasks. It also introduces JPEG compressibility objectives and four-reward alignment. Short-DrawBench is the retained DrawBench color subset under a new name; its larger test-set size is a protocol change.

E2.justification: The external comparator lineup remains Stable Diffusion, Rewarded Soup, CoDe, RGG and MORL. However, matched comparisons in Table 1 and Figure 2 now additionally evaluate DB-MPA-LS alongside DB-MPA, expanding the comparison lineup with the new proposed variant.

E3.justification: The main evaluation changes from 25 to 1,000 test prompts. New protocols include 550 GenEval training prompts with 700 held-out prompts, uniform-weight reward-count comparisons, and single-prompt SDXL fine-tuning with specified preference sweeps. These substantially expand evaluation design and model configurations.

E4.justification: Appendices C.3–C.7 add analyses of strongly conflicting rewards, scaling from two to four rewards, transfer to a larger SDXL backbone, and visual agreement between DB-MPA and its sampling approximation. These examine limitations and approximation quality beyond the earlier preference sweeps and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: v1 specifies 32 images per prompt with shared fixed seeds. v2 reports 30 seeds per prompt for retained training and three-reward evaluations, and 64 seeds per SDXL evaluation point, while omitting a general count for the expanded main tests. Neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests; these disclosures do not establish additional training replications.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the earlier test results: DB-MPA at w=0.5 changes from reward pair (0.70, 0.32) to (0.27, 0.21), under different test sets, not a demonstrated performance decline. v2 adds extensive results for the new scenarios and reports DB-MPA-LS at 5.64 versus DB-MPA's 11.11 seconds per image.

T1.justification: v2 adds a marginal-distribution equivalence proposition for random drift selection and its proof in Appendix A.4. It also corrects Proposition 1 from f_pre + u to f_pre - beta(t)u, propagating the scaling and sign corrections through Lemma 2 and Appendix A.3. The earlier general Proposition 2 is retained as Proposition 3.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion now present three algorithms and claim that DB-MPA-LS preserves approximately DB-MPA-level alignment while eliminating inference cost that scales linearly with the number of rewards. This adds a central efficiency contribution to the retained inference-time reward and KL alignment claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains the small training set through RL-convergence considerations, excludes sampling-based KL blending when coefficients are negative, and suggests VAE noise sensitivity explains CoDe's SDXL behavior. It removes v1's explicit memory limitation and distillation/parameter-sharing future directions. The warning about very small KL regularization remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds sampling pseudocode, prompt-generation instructions and SDXL training-time information. It removes the printed train/test prompt lists and explicit GPU-count/capacity details, referring readers to code for prompt lists. Existing optimizer and LoRA hyperparameters and the underlying code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds positioning against multi-LoRA composition, citing Zhong et al. (2024) and Zou et al. (2025) and contrasting heuristic scheduling with reward-aligned blending. Earlier diffusion-guidance, RL and LLM relationships are largely retained in condensed form.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable. v2 condenses related work and original algorithm descriptions, reorganizes experimental appendix subsections, shortens captions, updates author/conference text and adds an LLM-use disclosure. Much of the original explanatory prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands tables and figures for GenEval, conflicting rewards, reward scaling, SDXL and DB-MPA-LS, and restructures Table 1 and Figure 2. The prompt table and original Figure 5 comparison grids disappear. Earlier Table 3 and Figures 7–11 survive as Table 2 and Figures 8 and 12–15.

improvement.justification: The tested efficient variant, broader compositional evaluation and stress analyses substantially address v1's inference-cost and validation limitations, while corrected drift equations improve mathematical consistency. Reporting weaknesses temper these gains: prompt lists disappear, and some new aggregate scores are inconsistent—for example, Table 5's w=0.8 components imply 1.044 rather than the reported 0.88. These weaken exact effect-size claims but do not outweigh the substantial methodological and evidential improvements.
